findings.title: Rounded shading does not satisfy the raw-image volume comparison in Lemma 3.3

location.statement: Definition 3.2; equation (3.5) in Lemma 3.3; final multiplicity step

findings.claim_tested: Original union volume is comparable to rho^2 times the union of cubically rounded rescaled shadings after permitted refinement.
findings.complete_check: Fix epsilon=1/4, any eta>0, a=min(eta/2,1/8), rho=delta^(1/2), L=ceil(delta^-a), h=delta/rho. Directions on a K delta grid in a rho/1000 cap, all through zero, number J comparable to (rho/delta)^2. Shade each tube by one delta-grid cube in layers spaced L delta at heights 1/2 to 3/4. Tubes are essentially distinct and covered by a vertical rho-tube; all-scale angular nets have O(1) directional multiplicity. Cubes are disjoint, mu=1, and mass comparable to rho^2/L is at least delta^eta rho^2 for small delta. For every polylog-mass refinement E', one h-cube meets at most C/(L rho) images of its retained fine cubes and no images from two separated tubes. Thus |hat E'|>=c L rho^-2 |E'|, so rho^2|hat E'|/|E| grows at least L/polylog, contradicting (3.5). Full proof and geometric constants are in report F1.
counterevidence: Definition 3.2 explicitly rounds; Figure 1 shows cubes.
Input already has constant multiplicity; every allowed refinement still fails the volume comparison.
Example is not extremal and does not contradict Lemma 3.3's multiplicity conclusion.
The mu=1 example does not itself disprove the distinct final multiplicity equality.
The pointwise inequality mu*|Ehat|<=sum|Yhat| remains valid under cubical saturation because every occupied cube meets one point of constant original multiplicity mu.
Only this inequality is required in the inspected Lemma 3.3 / Proposition 3.2 Step 2 dependency; (3.5) can be deleted. Minor reflects redundancy in the actual derivation, not mere repairability.
findings.impact: The false rounded-volume equivalence (3.5) is stronger than the actual downstream requirement. The valid inequality mu*|Ehat|<=sum|Yhat| and the original parameter hierarchy restore the exact Lemma 3.3 conclusion used in Proposition 3.2 Step 2. No demonstrated core failure remains from this item; other steps are not newly certified.
findings.repair_status: Complete local multiplicity repair verified analytically: every rounded cube has at least mu retained tube incidences; N(s,t)<=sigma_n+epsilon/8 and s,t<=epsilon/4 give union volume >=h^(sigma_n+epsilon/4), while essential distinctness and a 2h-cover give total mass <=C*h^(-t). Hence mu<=h^(-sigma_n-epsilon) at a uniform small-scale threshold. Refinement mass loss and covering constants are absorbed by 2eta/epsilon<s,t. This does not restore the false volume equivalence or certify the entire proof.

focused_acceptance.reason: The complete separated multitube/layer family satisfies all covering and mass hypotheses and defeats (3.5) after every permitted polylog-mass refinement. It has multiplicity one and does not refute Lemma 3.3. The verified replacement is mu*|Ehat|<=sum|Yhat|, because every occupied coarse cube meets a raw-image point in mu distinct retained tube shadings. Choose N(s,t)<=sigma_n+epsilon/8 and s,t<=epsilon/4, then eta sufficiently small to absorb refinement and covering losses. The limsup lower bound |Ehat|>=h^(sigma_n+epsilon/4) and a 2h-cover upper bound sum|Yhat|<=C*h^(-t) give mu<=h^(-sigma_n-epsilon). Since delta<=h<=delta^epsilon, the threshold is uniform in rho. The exact downstream multiplicity conclusion holds within the original parameter hierarchy; no additional extremal hypothesis is used. F1 is Minor because the incorrect stronger equivalence is unnecessary in that derivation, not because repair is easy.

findings.title: Uniform projection proposition lacks intercept control
findings.claim_tested: For every epsilon a uniform delta0 works for all f with derivative conditions only.
findings.complete_check: Take epsilon=1/4, any delta<min(delta0,1/10), M=delta^-3, f(z)=M+z, and one vertical delta-tube. All derivative and direction hypotheses hold. The tube contains [-delta,delta]^2 times [-1,1]; its projected area is at least 4 delta (M+1), so the indicator L^(3/2) norm exceeds 4^(2/3) delta^(-4/3)>delta^(-5/4). This is a counterexample for every threshold. Exact rational test delta=1/256 saved.
counterevidence: Introductory outline assumes bounded C2 norm.
Adding f(0)=0 gives bounded f and uniform cinematic jet determinant 2 f'^2-f f''>=1.98.
findings.impact: False uniform statement is the final projection bound compared with Corollary 6.5 to force sigma=0.
findings.repair_status: Normalized local projection proof checked conditional on primary PYZ theorem statement. Full intercept-removing shear before Proposition 6.1 rescaling, including tube conventions and losses, remains pending.

focused_acceptance.reason: Proposition 7.1 chooses delta0 before arbitrary f and imposes derivative bounds only. For epsilon=1/4, any proposed threshold is defeated by delta<min(delta0,1/10), f(z)=delta^-3+z and one permitted vertical tube: projected area>=4delta(delta^-3+1), giving L^(3/2) norm>delta^(-5/4). The saved exact delta=1/256 inequality supports, but does not replace, this all-threshold argument. The introductory bounded-C2 outline and Lemma 7.3's explicit f(0)=0 are counterevidence; they are not hypotheses of Proposition 7.1. The normalized local repair remains conditional on the consulted primary cinematic theorem, and its preceding shear/tube/loss interface is not fully certified. The final contradiction explicitly uses this proposition against Corollary 6.5; Major is retained without a main-dimension-theorem disproof.

findings.title: Threshold grid construction can retain less than 1-c mass
findings.claim_tested: Discarding all cells of E-density below c loses less than c product mass.
findings.complete_check: Let c=1/10, G1 one square, G2 200 squares, E full on 179 product cells and density 1/20 on 21. With beta=0,K=1 every thin-tube inequality holds. Original E mass=3601/4000>=9/10; threshold construction retains 179/200<9/10. Thus the asserted mass of this construction is false.
counterevidence: Example does not disprove existence of a different discretized thin-tube set; beta=0 whole product works.
Discarded mass q obeys (1-c)q<=c, so retention >=1-2c for 0<c<1/2.
Neighborhood enlargement gives a verified thin-tube constant 5^beta K/c.
findings.impact: Requires corrected constants in discretized bootstrap; a fixed number of iterations changes a 3^N loss to a 6^N loss absorbable into a smaller scale threshold.
findings.repair_status: Local weaker replacement proved. Exact original retention 1-c not recovered; full bootstrap and Lemma 8.8 still pending.

focused_acceptance.reason: For c=1/10 and beta=0,K=1, one first grid square and 200 second grid squares with 179 full product cells and 21 of density 1/20 satisfy every thin-tube condition. The initial mass is 3601/4000>=9/10, whereas the specified threshold retains 179/200<9/10. This refutes the construction's claimed mass, not existence of some alternative discretization. The discarded mass q satisfies (1-c)q<=c, giving retention>=1-2c, and the neighbourhood proof yields 5^beta*K/c. Fixed-many-step losses of type 6^N*c can be absorbed by a smaller power threshold. Minor and this limited repair are retained; exact 1-c retention and the full Section 8 proof remain uncertified.
